title: Judaism: covenant
hookLine: a people bound to God through Abraham, Sinai and the Torah

lines: A BOND TO COME BACK TO.
cards: Think of the difference between a contract and a marriage. A contract says: if you do this, I'll do that, and if you don't, we're done.
A marriage says something stranger: we belong to each other now, through good years and bad, and even when one of us fails, the bond is still there to come back to.
Jews have a word for the relationship between God and the Jewish people, much closer to the second than the first. It runs through the whole Hebrew Bible. Today's word: brit.

teach.b: Brit is Hebrew for covenant, a binding promise between two parties. The Torah tells of several.
After the flood, God makes a covenant with Noah and every living thing, never again to destroy the earth by flood, and sets a rainbow in the clouds as its sign.
Jewish tradition sees that covenant as embracing all humanity. Then Abraham.

God promises him descendants as many as the stars and a land for them, and the sign is circumcision, brit milah, still performed for Jewish baby boys on the eighth day, which is why many people know the word as bris.
Then Sinai, the great one. The people, freed from Egypt, stand at the foot of the mountain.
Moses reads them the book of the covenant, and in the Jewish Publication Society's 1917 translation they answer: "All that the LORD hath spoken will we do, and obey."

teach.h: SINAI: WE WILL DO, AND HEAR.
teach.b: In Hebrew, naaseh venishma: literally, we will do, and we will hear. The rabbis of the Talmud loved that order: doing before fully understanding, like people in love who say yes before they know every detail.
At Sinai the covenant is the Torah itself, the teaching and the commandments, a whole way of life given and received.
And Deuteronomy says it was made not only with those standing there that day, but with those not yet there. Many Jews understand that to include every Jewish generation since.
The covenant runs two ways: God bound to a people, and a people bound to God. Jews have argued with it, struggled with it and wept over it for thousands of years.

how: Jews understand their life of Torah and commandments as living within the covenant; brit milah, circumcision on the eighth day, marks a baby boy's entry into the covenant of Abraham, and many communities hold a naming ceremony for girls.

games.q: you're standing at the foot of Sinai. Moses reads the book of the covenant aloud. how do the people answer?
o: we will do, and we will hear.
games.why: they say: all that the LORD hath spoken will we do, and obey. in Hebrew, naaseh venishma, we will do and we will hear, doing before fully understanding.

practice: Think of one commitment that has lasted, not one you broke: to a person, a family, a friend, a community, a craft, a faith. Remember how it began, and a hard stretch when keeping it cost you something.
Notice what it's made of you, the weight of it and the steadiness.

wordCard.voice: Brit. Hebrew for covenant: the binding bond between God and the Jewish people, through Abraham, Sinai and the Torah. Today's word.
